title: Honey Mustard Roast Chicken
subtitle: British roast chicken with a sticky honey and mustard glaze
excerpt: This is a straightforward roast chicken with a glaze that turns golden and sticky in the oven. Honey and Dijon mustard are mixed with butter and applied generously before the bird goes in. A rest after roasting keeps the meat juicy.
sourceNotes: Classic British roast chicken technique with a honey mustard glaze. The combination is a household favourite across the UK.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The glaze can be mixed and refrigerated a day ahead.

content.text: Take the chicken out of the fridge 30 minutes before roasting. Cold chicken straight from the fridge cooks unevenly. Resting the bird after roasting allows the juices to settle back through the meat.

items.prepNote: 1 halved and put inside the cavity, 1 cut into wedges to serve

content.text: Mix the honey, mustard, and softened butter in a small bowl until smooth.
Place the chicken in the roasting tin. Tuck the thyme sprigs and garlic halves around it. Put the halved lemon inside the cavity.
Spoon the glaze all over the chicken. Get it under the skin on the breast if you can.
Season the outside generously with salt and pepper.
Roast for 75 to 80 minutes. The juices should run clear when you pierce the thigh at its thickest point.
If the skin is getting too dark before the chicken is done, loosely tent with foil and continue roasting.
Rest the chicken in a warm place for 15 minutes before carving. Serve with lemon wedges.

items.symptom: Glaze is burning before chicken is cooked
items.cause: Oven too hot or chicken too high in the oven
items.fix: Tent with foil and move to a lower shelf.
Check temperature at 75 minutes and always rest for 15 minutes.

items.symptom: Skin is pale and not crispy
items.cause: Oven not hot enough or bird too wet going in
items.fix: Pat the skin dry before adding the glaze.
